notes: Sentences a Colombian backend developer would plausibly say at work,
each carrying exactly one planted error. One error per sample on
purpose: with two, a transcript that repairs one and keeps the other
cannot be scored without judgement, and judgement is what this
experiment is trying to avoid needing.
`error` is the normalised substring that has to appear for the mistake
to have survived transcription. `repaired` lists the substrings that
mean Whisper wrote the grammatical form instead. Anything else is
reported verbatim as `other`, because a transcript that says neither
is an ASR failure and not a fidelity result.
The controls are already correct. They measure the opposite risk: an
error the transcriber invents becomes a lesson about a mistake the

samples.spoken: Yesterday I go to the office and I speak with my manager about the project.
Since three months I am learning about Kubernetes and Terraform.
samples.error: since three months i am learning
repaired: for three months i have been learning
for the last three months i have been learning
for three months i am learning

samples.spoken: I have twenty eight years and I work as a backend developer.
I need to fix a problem very complex in the queue consumer.
Do you know where is the staging server?
I have to assist to the sprint review at nine in the morning.
The client is very sensible about the response times.
samples.note: sensible is an English word, so nothing forces a repair. Included as the case the transcript should keep and the assessor has to catch on meaning, not on grammar.
